steps.observation: You have 60 seconds. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action:
Think of a Transformer as a stack of identical layers that learn to “mix” information from every position in a sequence all at once, instead of step-by-step like an RNN. Here’s the rough idea in under a minute:

1. Input Embeddings + Positional Encodings  
   • Each token turns into a vector.  
   • We add a fixed or learned positional vector so the model “knows” token order.

2. Multi-Head Self-Attention  
   • For each token, compute three vectors—Query (Q), Key (K), Value (V)—by linear projection.  
   • Compute attention scores = softmax(Q·Kᵀ/√d). This tells you how much each token cares about every other.  
   • Multiply scores by V to get a new, context-aware representation.  
   • “Multi-head” means you do several of these in parallel, then concatenate and project back.

3. Add & Norm  
   • Add the original input (“residual connection”) to the attention output.  
   • Apply layer normalization to stabilize training.

4. Feed-Forward Network  
   • A small two-layer MLP (with a nonlinearity) applied independently to each position.  
   • Another add & norm step.

5. Stack Layers  
   • Repeat steps 2–4 N times (e.g. 6–12 layers).

6. (For Decoding)  
   • Masked self-attention so each position only attends to earlier ones.  
   • Extra encoder–decoder attention to bring in source information.

7. Final Linear + Softmax  
   • Project decoder outputs to vocabulary size and apply softmax to get next-token probabilities.

Key takeaway: at every layer, each token “re-weights” information from every other token via dot-product attention, building rich contextual embeddings in parallel.
